title: Cult.fit Wins SEBI Clearance for IPO Built on ₹950 Crore Fresh Issue
excerpt: The fitness chain's losses halved in FY26 as revenue rose 41.5% to ₹1,720.6 crore; early backers including Temasek and Accel will sell shares in an offer expected to total about ₹4,000 crore.
body:
• SEBI issued its final observations on Cult.fit's offer documents on October 12, clearing the fitness chain to proceed with its public issue roughly three months after it filed its DRHP in July.
  • The IPO combines a fresh issue of up to ₹950 crore (about $100 million) with an offer for sale of up to 17.86 crore shares; the total issue size is expected to be around ₹4,000 crore.
  • Cult.fit narrowed its FY26 net loss to ₹251.8 crore from ₹480.8 crore in FY25, on operating revenue up 41.5% to ₹1,720.6 crore; it runs 708 centres in 77 cities with 9.87 lakh paid members.
  • Temasek, Schroders Capital, Accel, Tata Digital and cofounder Mukesh Bansal are among the shareholders selling in the OFS; Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs, Jefferies, JM Financial and Morgan Stanley India run the issue.

India's largest gym chain is headed to the public markets. The Securities and Exchange Board of India has given Cult.fit its go-ahead for an initial public offering built around a ₹950 crore fresh issue, Reuters reported on Friday, after the regulator issued its final observations on the company's draft papers on October 12.

The shape of the issue

Cult.fit filed its draft red herring prospectus in July. Alongside the fresh issue, existing shareholders will sell up to 17.86 crore shares through an offer for sale, taking the expected total issue size to about ₹4,000 crore, according to Inc42. The selling shareholders include Temasek (through MacRitchie Investments), Schroders Capital, German fitness operator LifeFit Group, Accel, Tata Digital and cofounder Mukesh Bansal. The fresh-issue money is earmarked for new fitness centres, lease and licence costs on existing centres, repayment of borrowings, new exclusive brand outlets for its Cultsport products business, and marketing.

A turnaround story to sell

The numbers Cult.fit takes to investors are much improved. FY26 net loss narrowed to ₹251.8 crore from ₹480.8 crore a year earlier, while operating revenue rose 41.5% to ₹1,720.6 crore, and adjusted EBITDA margin turned positive at about 8.4%. The network spans 708 centres across 77 cities — 218 owned and operated, the rest franchised or independently owned — with more than 9.87 lakh paid members as of March 31, 2026. Fitness services contribute roughly 70% of revenue and products about 30%. Founded in 2016 as Curefit, the company has raised more than $800 million from investors including Zomato, Accel, Kalaari Capital and Chiratae Ventures.

What to watch

SEBI's observation is a clearance, not a launch date: the company must still file its red herring prospectus with the price band and issue dates. For NRI investors, the practical step is to watch for the RHP, since NRI participation runs through the standard non-institutional/resident-equivalent routes depending on the account type used. The listing also lands in a crowded Indian IPO calendar, where fitness is a new category for public investors — the draft papers cite a Redseer estimate putting India's fitness services market at ₹25,600 crore in CY25, roughly doubling by CY30. Whether public markets pay a platform multiple for a business that is still loss-making will be the issue's real test.
